title: QUIZ - 105
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the elements in A \ B for given finite sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3,4\}\) and \(B=\{3,4,5\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \setminus B\) contains elements in A but not in B. Removing 3 and 4 from A leaves \(\{1,2\}\).
questions.hint: List the elements of A and remove those that also appear in B.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the elements in B \ A for given finite sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{2,4,6\}\) and \(B=\{4,6,8\}\), what is \(B \setminus A\)?
questions.explanation: \(B \setminus A\) contains elements in B but not in A. Only 8 is in B and not in A.
questions.hint: Start with B and remove any element that also belongs to A.

questions.learningObjective: Find the set difference of two sets of letters.
questions.question: If \(A=\{a,b,c\}\) and \(B=\{b,d\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Remove b from A because b is in B. The remaining elements are a and c.
questions.hint: Keep only elements of A that are not in B.

questions.learningObjective: Compute A \ B for numerical sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,3,5,7\}\) and \(B=\{2,3,5\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Elements 3 and 5 are in both sets, so they are removed from A. The result is \(\{1,7\}\).
questions.hint: Check which elements appear in both sets and exclude them.

questions.learningObjective: Determine A \ B when B contains one element of A.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2\}\) and \(B=\{2,3\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Only 2 is in both A and B, so it is removed from A. The remaining element is 1.
questions.hint: Remove from A any element that is also in B.

questions.learningObjective: Find A \ B for small sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{x,y,z\}\) and \(B=\{y\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Remove y from A because y is in B. The remaining elements are x and z.
questions.hint: Subtract the elements of B from A.

questions.learningObjective: Compute A \ B for even-number sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{2,4,6,8\}\) and \(B=\{4,6\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Remove 4 and 6 from A. The remaining elements are 2 and 8.
questions.hint: Identify the common elements and exclude them from A.

questions.learningObjective: Determine B \ A for given sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{3,4,5\}\), what is \(B \setminus A\)?
questions.explanation: Elements 4 and 5 are in B but not in A. So \(B \setminus A=\{4,5\}\).
questions.hint: Start with B and remove elements that are also in A.

questions.learningObjective: Find A \ B when one element is shared.
questions.question: If \(A=\{a,c,e\}\) and \(B=\{a,b,c\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Remove a and c from A because they are in B. Only e remains.
questions.hint: Keep elements of A that are not in B.

questions.learningObjective: Compute A \ B for numerical sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,4,7\}\) and \(B=\{4,7,9\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Remove 4 and 7 from A. The only remaining element is 1.
questions.hint: Exclude any element of A that also belongs to B.

questions.learningObjective: Determine A \ B for prime-number sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{2,3,5,7\}\) and \(B=\{3,5\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Remove 3 and 5 from A. The remaining elements are 2 and 7.
questions.hint: Subtract the common elements from A.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize when B \ A is empty.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3,4\}\) and \(B=\{1,3\}\), what is \(B \setminus A\)?
questions.explanation: Every element of B is already in A, so removing A from B leaves the empty set.
questions.hint: Check whether B has any element that is not in A.

questions.learningObjective: Find A \ B for letter sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{p,q,r\}\) and \(B=\{q,s\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Remove q from A because q is in B. The remaining elements are p and r.
questions.hint: Keep only elements of A that are not in B.

questions.learningObjective: Compute A \ B for multiples of ten.
questions.question: If \(A=\{10,20,30\}\) and \(B=\{20,40\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Remove 20 from A. The remaining elements are 10 and 30.
questions.hint: Exclude elements that are in both sets.

questions.learningObjective: Determine A \ B when one element is shared.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,5,9\}\) and \(B=\{5,6,9\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Remove 5 and 9 from A because they are in B. Only 1 remains.
questions.hint: List A and delete elements that also appear in B.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize when A \ B is empty.
questions.question: If \(A=\{x,y\}\) and \(B=\{x,y,z\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: All elements of A are also in B, so \(A \setminus B\) is empty.
questions.hint: Check whether every element of A is also in B.

questions.learningObjective: Find the complement of a set relative to a universal set.
questions.question: If \(U=\{1,2,3,4,5\}\) and \(A=\{1,3\}\), what is \(A^c\)?
questions.explanation: \(A^c\) contains elements of U that are not in A. These are 2, 4, and 5.
questions.hint: List the elements of U and remove those in A.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection of two sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2\}\) and \(B=\{2,3\}\), what is \(A \cap B\)?
questions.explanation: The intersection contains elements common to both sets. Only 2 is in both A and B.
questions.hint: Look for elements that appear in both sets.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the union of two sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2\}\) and \(B=\{2,3\}\), what is \(A \cup B\)?
questions.explanation: The union contains all elements in either set. Combining A and B gives \(\{1,2,3\}\).
questions.hint: Combine all elements without repeating 2.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the difference of two sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{4,5\}\) and \(B=\{5,6\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \setminus B\) removes elements of B from A. A has 4, 5; removing 5 (which is in B) leaves \(\{4\}\).
questions.hint: Remove any elements of B from A.

questions.learningObjective: Find the complement of a union.
questions.question: If \(U=\{1,2,3,4\}\), \(A=\{1,2\}\), and \(B=\{2,3\}\), what is \((A \cup B)^c\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \cup B=\{1,2,3\}\). Its complement in U is \(\{4\}\).
questions.hint: First find the union, then remove it from the universal set.

questions.learningObjective: Find the complement of an intersection.
questions.question: If \(U=\{1,2,3,4\}\), \(A=\{1,2\}\), and \(B=\{2,3\}\), what is \((A \cap B)^c\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \cap B=\{2\}\). Its complement in U is \(\{1,3,4\}\).
questions.hint: First find the intersection, then remove it from U.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret membership in an intersection.
questions.question: What does \(x \in A \cap B\) mean?
questions.explanation: An element is in the intersection if it belongs to both sets.
questions.hint: Think of intersection as the overlap of two sets.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret membership in a union.
questions.question: What does \(x \in A \cup B\) mean?
questions.explanation: An element is in the union if it belongs to at least one of the sets.
questions.hint: Think of union as combining the sets.

questions.learningObjective: Apply De Morgan's law for union.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \((A \cup B)^c\)?
questions.explanation: By De Morgan's law, the complement of a union is the intersection of the complements.
questions.hint: Recall how complement interacts with union.

questions.learningObjective: Apply De Morgan's law for intersection.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \((A \cap B)^c\)?
questions.explanation: By De Morgan's law, the complement of an intersection is the union of the complements.
questions.hint: Recall how complement interacts with intersection.

questions.learningObjective: Compute an intersection.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{3,4\}\), what is \(A \cap B\)?
questions.explanation: The only common element is 3.
questions.hint: Find elements that appear in both sets.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a union.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{3,4\}\), what is \(A \cup B\)?
questions.explanation: The union combines all elements from A and B.
questions.hint: List all elements from both sets without repetition.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize disjoint sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2\}\) and \(B=\{3,4\}\), what is \(A \cap B\)?
questions.explanation: The sets have no common elements, so their intersection is empty.
questions.hint: Check whether any element appears in both sets.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the union of disjoint sets.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2\}\) and \(B=\{3,4\}\), what is \(A \cup B\)?
questions.explanation: The union contains all elements from both sets.
questions.hint: Combine the elements of A and B.

questions.learningObjective: Find the intersection of two complements.
questions.question: If \(U=\{1,2,3,4,5\}\), \(A=\{1,2\}\), and \(B=\{2,3\}\), what is \(A^c \cap B^c\)?
questions.hint: First find each complement, then take the common elements.

questions.learningObjective: Find the union of two complements.
questions.question: If \(U=\{1,2,3,4,5\}\), \(A=\{1,2\}\), and \(B=\{2,3\}\), what is \(A^c \cup B^c\)?
questions.hint: Combine the elements of both complements.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a set difference.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{3,4,5\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Remove 3 from A because it is in B. The remaining elements are 1 and 2.
questions.hint: Keep elements of A that are not in B.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a set difference.
questions.question: If \(A=\{5,6,7\}\) and \(B=\{7,8,9\}\), what is \(B \setminus A\)?
questions.explanation: \(B \setminus A\) removes elements of A from B. B has 7, 8, 9; removing 7 (which is in A) leaves \(\{8,9\}\).
questions.hint: Remove any elements of A from B.

questions.learningObjective: Compute an intersection.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{3,4,5\}\), what is \(A \cap B\)?
questions.explanation: The only common element is 3.
questions.hint: Find the overlap of A and B.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a union.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{3,4,5\}\), what is \(A \cup B\)?
questions.explanation: The union combines all elements from both sets.
questions.hint: List all elements from A and B without repetition.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret complement membership.
questions.question: What does \(x \in A^c\) mean?
questions.explanation: The complement of A contains elements not in A.
questions.hint: Think of complement as the opposite of belonging to A.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret set difference membership.
questions.question: What does \(x \in A \setminus B\) mean?
questions.explanation: Set difference contains elements in A that are not in B.
questions.hint: Think of removing B from A.

questions.learningObjective: Analyze a set identity.
questions.question: What is \((A \setminus B) \cap B\)?
questions.explanation: Elements in \(A \setminus B\) are not in B, so the intersection with B is empty.
questions.hint: Consider whether an element can be both in B and not in B.

questions.learningObjective: Analyze a set identity.
questions.question: What is \((A \setminus B) \cup (A \cap B)\)?
questions.explanation: Together, \(A \setminus B\) and \(A \cap B\) cover exactly all elements of A.
questions.hint: Split A into elements in B and elements not in B.

questions.learningObjective: Compute an intersection.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3,4\}\) and \(B=\{3,4,5,6\}\), what is \(A \cap B\)?
questions.explanation: The common elements are 3 and 4.
questions.hint: Find elements that appear in both sets.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a union.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3,4\}\) and \(B=\{3,4,5,6\}\), what is \(A \cup B\)?
questions.explanation: The union contains all elements from both sets.
questions.hint: Combine all elements without repeating 3 and 4.

questions.learningObjective: Find a complement.
questions.question: If \(U=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\) and \(A=\{1,3,5\}\), what is \(A^c\)?
questions.explanation: The elements of U not in A are 2, 4, and 6.
questions.hint: Remove the odd numbers in A from U.

questions.learningObjective: Compute an intersection.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,3,5\}\) and \(B=\{2,4,6\}\), what is \(A \cap B\)?
questions.explanation: The sets have no common elements.
questions.hint: Check whether any number appears in both sets.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a union.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,3,5\}\) and \(B=\{2,4,6\}\), what is \(A \cup B\)?
questions.explanation: The union contains all elements from both sets.
questions.hint: Combine the odd and even numbers.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound set expression.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2\}\), \(B=\{2,3\}\), and \(C=\{3,4\}\), what is \(A \cap (B \cup C)\)?
questions.explanation: \(B \cup C=\{2,3,4\}\). Intersecting with A gives \(\{2\}\).
questions.hint: First find \(B \cup C\), then intersect with A.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound set expression.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2\}\), \(B=\{2,3\}\), and \(C=\{3,4\}\), what is \((A \cap B) \cup C\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \cap B=\{2\}\). Union with C gives \(\{2,3,4\}\).
questions.hint: First find \(A \cap B\), then union with C.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound set expression.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2\}\), \(B=\{2,3\}\), and \(C=\{3,4\}\), what is \(A \cup (B \cap C)\)?
questions.explanation: \(B \cap C=\{3\}\). Union with A gives \(\{1,2,3\}\).
questions.hint: First find \(B \cap C\), then union with A.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound set expression.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2\}\), \(B=\{2,3\}\), and \(C=\{3,4\}\), what is \((A \cup B) \cap C\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \cup B=\{1,2,3\}\). Intersecting with C gives \(\{3\}\).
questions.hint: First find \(A \cup B\), then intersect with C.

questions.learningObjective: Find the complement of a set difference.
questions.question: If \(U=\{1,2,3,4,5\}\), \(A=\{1,2\}\), and \(B=\{2,3\}\), what is \((A \setminus B)^c\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \setminus B=\{1\}\). Its complement in U is \(\{2,3,4,5\}\).
questions.hint: First find \(A \setminus B\), then remove it from U.

questions.learningObjective: Find the complement of a set difference.
questions.question: If \(U=\{1,2,3,4,5\}\), \(A=\{1,2\}\), and \(B=\{2,3\}\), what is \((B \setminus A)^c\)?
questions.explanation: \(B \setminus A=\{3\}\). Its complement in U is \(\{1,2,4,5\}\).
questions.hint: First find \(B \setminus A\), then remove it from U.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize commutativity of intersection.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(A \cap B\)?
questions.explanation: Intersection is commutative, so \(A \cap B = B \cap A\).
questions.hint: Think about the order of the sets in an intersection.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize commutativity of union.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(A \cup B\)?
questions.explanation: Union is commutative, so \(A \cup B = B \cup A\).
questions.hint: Think about the order of the sets in a union.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a set difference.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{2,3,4\}\), what is \(A \setminus B\)?
questions.explanation: Remove 2 and 3 from A. Only 1 remains.
questions.hint: Keep elements of A that are not in B.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a set difference.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{2,3,4\}\), what is \(B \setminus A\)?
questions.explanation: Remove 2 and 3 from B. Only 4 remains.
questions.hint: Keep elements of B that are not in A.

questions.learningObjective: Compute an intersection.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{2,3,4\}\), what is \(A \cap B\)?
questions.explanation: The common elements are 2 and 3.
questions.hint: Find the overlap of A and B.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a union.
questions.question: If \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{2,3,4\}\), what is \(A \cup B\)?
questions.explanation: The union contains all elements from both sets.
questions.hint: Combine all elements without repeating 2 and 3.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of a single coin toss.
questions.question: What is the sample space when a fair coin is tossed once?
questions.explanation: A single coin toss has two possible outcomes: heads or tails.
questions.hint: Consider the two possible results of one coin toss.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of a die roll.
questions.question: What is the sample space when a fair six-sided die is rolled once?
questions.explanation: A six-sided die can land on any integer from 1 to 6.
questions.hint: List all possible faces of a standard die.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of two coin tosses.
questions.question: What is the sample space when two distinguishable coins are tossed?
questions.explanation: Each coin has two outcomes, giving four ordered pairs.
questions.hint: List all combinations of heads and tails for two coins.

questions.learningObjective: Identify possible sums when rolling two dice.
questions.question: When two fair dice are rolled, what are the possible sums?
questions.explanation: The smallest sum is 1+1=2 and the largest is 6+6=12.
questions.hint: Think about the minimum and maximum possible sums.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of a spinner.
questions.question: A spinner has three colors: red, blue, and green. What is the sample space for one spin?
questions.explanation: The possible outcomes are the three colors on the spinner.
questions.hint: List all colors shown on the spinner.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of card suits.
questions.question: A card is drawn from a standard deck and its suit is recorded. What is the sample space?
questions.explanation: A standard deck has four suits: hearts, diamonds, clubs, and spades.
questions.hint: List the four suits in a deck of cards.

questions.learningObjective: Count outcomes of a two-step experiment.
questions.question: A coin is tossed and a die is rolled. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.explanation: The coin has 2 outcomes and the die has 6, so \(2 \times 6 = 12\).
questions.hint: Multiply the number of outcomes for each step.

questions.learningObjective: Count ordered outcomes of rolling two dice.
questions.question: A die is rolled twice. How many ordered outcomes are possible?
questions.explanation: Each roll has 6 outcomes, so \(6 \times 6 = 36\).
questions.hint: Multiply the outcomes of the first roll by the outcomes of the second.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of choosing a letter.
questions.question: A letter is chosen at random from the word MATH. What is the sample space?
questions.explanation: The distinct letters in MATH are M, A, T, and H.
questions.hint: List each different letter in the word.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of drawing a colored ball.
questions.question: A bag contains red, blue, and green balls. One ball is drawn. What is the sample space?
questions.explanation: The possible colors are red, blue, and green.
questions.hint: List all colors present in the bag.

questions.learningObjective: Count outcomes of three coin tosses.
questions.question: Three fair coins are tossed. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.explanation: Each coin has 2 outcomes, so \(2^3 = 8\).
questions.hint: Multiply 2 by itself three times.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an outcome from a sample space.
questions.question: A die is rolled once. Which of the following is an outcome?
questions.explanation: An outcome is a single possible result, such as 4.
questions.hint: An outcome is one result, not the whole set.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of one coin toss.
questions.question: A coin is tossed once. Which of the following is the sample space?
questions.explanation: The sample space lists all possible outcomes: heads and tails.
questions.hint: The sample space is the set of all possible results.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an event as a subset of outcomes.
questions.question: A die is rolled. Which set represents the event of getting an even number?
questions.explanation: The even numbers on a die are 2, 4, and 6.
questions.hint: List the even faces of a standard die.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an outcome from a sample space.
questions.question: Two coins are tossed. Which of the following is an outcome?
questions.explanation: HT is one possible result of tossing two coins.
questions.hint: An outcome is a single result, not the entire sample space.

questions.learningObjective: Identify sample space by color.
questions.question: A bag has 3 red marbles and 2 blue marbles. One marble is drawn and its color is noted. What is the sample space?
questions.explanation: The possible colors are red and blue.
questions.hint: List the different colors in the bag.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of a die roll.
questions.question: What is the sample space for rolling a fair six-sided die?
questions.explanation: A standard die has faces numbered 1 through 6.
questions.hint: Include every face of the die.

questions.learningObjective: Count outcomes of two coin tosses.
questions.question: Two coins are tossed. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.explanation: Each coin has 2 outcomes, so \(2 \times 2 = 4\).
questions.hint: Multiply the number of outcomes for each coin.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of a spinner.
questions.question: A spinner has numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4. What is the sample space for one spin?
questions.explanation: The possible outcomes are the four numbers on the spinner.
questions.hint: List all numbers on the spinner.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of days of the week.
questions.question: A day of the week is chosen at random. What is the sample space?
questions.explanation: There are seven days in a week, so all seven must be listed.
questions.hint: List every day of the week.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an impossible outcome.
questions.question: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. Which result is NOT in the sample space?
questions.explanation: A six-sided die has outcomes 1 through 6, so 7 is impossible.
questions.hint: Check the possible faces of a standard die.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an outcome not in the sample space.
questions.question: Two coins are tossed. Which of the following is NOT an outcome?
questions.explanation: Tossing two coins gives two-letter outcomes such as HH, HT, TH, and TT. HHH has three letters.
questions.hint: Count the number of coin results in each option.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of drawing a number.
questions.question: A bag contains cards numbered 1, 2, and 3. One card is drawn. What is the sample space?
questions.explanation: The possible outcomes are the numbers 1, 2, and 3.
questions.hint: List all numbers on the cards.

questions.learningObjective: Count outcomes of a die roll.
questions.question: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.explanation: The die has six faces, so there are 6 outcomes.
questions.hint: Count the faces on a standard die.

questions.learningObjective: Count outcomes of a coin toss and die roll.
questions.question: A coin is tossed and a die is rolled. How many outcomes are possible?
questions.explanation: The coin has 2 outcomes and the die has 6, so \(2 \times 6 = 12\).
questions.hint: Multiply the number of outcomes for each experiment.

questions.learningObjective: Count ordered outcomes of two dice.
questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. How many ordered outcomes are possible?
questions.explanation: Each die has 6 outcomes, so \(6 \times 6 = 36\).
questions.hint: Multiply the outcomes of the first die by the outcomes of the second.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of drawing a colored object.
questions.question: A jar contains red, green, blue, and yellow balls. One ball is drawn. What is the sample space?
questions.explanation: The possible colors are red, green, blue, and yellow.
questions.hint: List all colors present in the jar.

questions.learningObjective: Count outcomes of three coin tosses.
questions.question: A coin is tossed three times. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.explanation: Each toss has 2 outcomes, so \(2^3 = 8\).
questions.hint: Multiply 2 by itself three times.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an event from a die roll.
questions.question: A die is rolled. Which set represents the event of getting a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: Numbers greater than 4 on a die are 5 and 6.
questions.hint: List the faces that are strictly greater than 4.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of a spinner.
questions.question: A spinner has numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. What is the sample space for one spin?
questions.explanation: The possible outcomes are the five numbers on the spinner.
questions.hint: List all numbers shown on the spinner.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an outcome from a sample space.
questions.question: A coin is tossed once. Which of the following is an outcome?
questions.explanation: T is a single possible result of one coin toss.
questions.hint: An outcome is one result, not the whole set.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an outcome from a sample space.
questions.question: A die is rolled once. Which of the following is an outcome?
questions.explanation: 3 is one possible result of rolling a die.
questions.hint: An outcome is a single result.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a possible outcome.
questions.question: Two coins are tossed. Which of the following is a possible outcome?
questions.explanation: With two coins, outcomes have two letters. HT is possible.
questions.hint: Count the number of coin results in each option.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of ordered pairs from two dice.
questions.question: Two dice are rolled and the ordered pair of results is recorded. What is the sample space?
questions.explanation: Each roll gives a number from 1 to 6, and order matters, so all ordered pairs are included.
questions.hint: Think of each outcome as a pair of numbers.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space by color.
questions.question: A bag has 5 red marbles and 3 blue marbles. One marble is drawn and its color is noted. What is the sample space?
questions.explanation: The possible colors are red and blue.
questions.hint: List the different colors in the bag.

questions.learningObjective: Count outcomes of four coin tosses.
questions.question: A coin is tossed four times. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.explanation: Each toss has 2 outcomes, so \(2^4 = 16\).
questions.hint: Multiply 2 by itself four times.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an event from a die roll.
questions.question: A die is rolled. Which set represents the event of getting an odd number?
questions.explanation: The odd numbers on a die are 1, 3, and 5.
questions.hint: List the odd faces of a standard die.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of choosing a number.
questions.question: A number from 1 to 5 is chosen at random. What is the sample space?
questions.explanation: The possible outcomes are the numbers 1 through 5.
questions.hint: List all integers from 1 to 5.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sample space of two coin tosses.
questions.question: Two coins are tossed. Which of the following is the sample space?
questions.explanation: All four ordered combinations must be included.
questions.hint: List every possible pair of heads and tails.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an event from an outcome.
questions.question: A die is rolled. Which of the following is an event?
questions.explanation: An event is a set of outcomes. \(\{2,4,6\}\) is a subset of the sample space.
questions.hint: An event is a collection of outcomes, not a single result.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret an event from a die roll.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\{2,4,6\}\) represents:
questions.explanation: The outcomes 2, 4, and 6 are the even numbers on a die.
questions.hint: Look at the parity of the numbers in E.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret an event from a coin toss.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{H,T\}\). The event \(E=\{H\}\) represents:
questions.explanation: The outcome H represents heads.
questions.hint: Match the letter in the event to the coin result.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret an event from a die roll.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\{1,3,5\}\) represents:
questions.explanation: The outcomes 1, 3, and 5 are the odd numbers on a die.
questions.hint: Check whether the numbers in E are odd or even.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret an event from two coin tosses.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}\). The event \(E=\{HH,HT\}\) represents:
questions.explanation: In both HH and HT, the first letter is H, meaning the first toss is heads.
questions.hint: Look at the first letter in each outcome of E.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret an event from a color sample space.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{\text{red},\text{blue},\text{green}\}\). The event \(E=\{\text{red}\}\) represents:
questions.explanation: The event contains only the outcome red.
questions.hint: Match the color in the event to the description.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether an event is simple.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\{6\}\) is:
questions.explanation: A simple event contains exactly one outcome. Here E contains only 6.
questions.hint: Count the number of outcomes in the event.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether an event is compound.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\{2,4,6\}\) is:
questions.explanation: A compound event contains more than one outcome. E has three outcomes.
questions.hint: Check whether the event has more than one element.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an impossible event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event of rolling a 7 is:
questions.explanation: 7 is not in the sample space, so the event cannot occur.
questions.hint: Check whether 7 is a possible outcome on a die.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a certain event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event of rolling a number less than 7 is:
questions.explanation: Every outcome in S is less than 7, so the event is certain.
questions.hint: Compare all possible outcomes with the condition.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a certain event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{H,T\}\). The event \(E=\{H,T\}\) is:
questions.explanation: E contains all outcomes in the sample space, so it is certain.
questions.hint: Check whether the event includes every possible outcome.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a certain event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\) is:
questions.explanation: E equals the entire sample space, so it is certain.
questions.hint: Compare the event with the sample space.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an impossible event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\emptyset\) is:
questions.explanation: The empty set contains no outcomes, so the event cannot occur.
questions.hint: Think about what an event with no outcomes means.

questions.learningObjective: Determine if an outcome belongs to an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event is \(E=\{2,4,6\}\). Which outcome is in E?
questions.explanation: 4 is listed in E. 3 is not.
questions.hint: Check which number appears in the set E.

questions.learningObjective: Determine if an outcome belongs to an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}\). The event is \(E=\{HT,TH\}\). Which outcome is in E?
questions.explanation: HT is listed in E. HH is not.
questions.hint: Check which outcome appears in the set E.

questions.learningObjective: Determine if an outcome is not in an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event is \(E=\{1,3,5\}\). Which outcome is NOT in E?
questions.explanation: 2 is not in E, while 1 is in E.
questions.hint: Look for the number that is missing from E.

questions.learningObjective: Determine if an outcome is not in an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{\text{red},\text{blue},\text{green}\}\). The event is \(E=\{\text{red},\text{blue}\}\). Which outcome is NOT in E?
questions.explanation: Green is not in E, while red is in E.
questions.hint: Find the color that is not listed in E.

questions.learningObjective: Find the complement of an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event is \(E=\{2,4,6\}\). What is the complement of E?
questions.explanation: The complement contains outcomes in S but not in E, which are 1, 3, and 5.
questions.hint: List the outcomes of S that are not in E.

questions.learningObjective: Find the complement of an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{H,T\}\). The event is \(E=\{H\}\). What is the complement of E?
questions.explanation: The only outcome not in E is T.
questions.hint: List the outcome of S that is not H.

questions.learningObjective: Find the complement of an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event is \(E=\{1,2\}\). What is the complement of E?
questions.explanation: The outcomes not in E are 3, 4, 5, and 6.
questions.hint: Remove 1 and 2 from the sample space.

questions.learningObjective: Find the complement of an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}\). The event is \(E=\{HH,HT,TH\}\). What is the complement of E?
questions.explanation: The only outcome not in E is TT.
questions.hint: Find the outcome of S that is missing from E.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret an event from a die roll.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\{5,6\}\) represents:
questions.explanation: 5 and 6 are both greater than 4.
questions.hint: Compare each outcome in E with the number 4.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret an event from a die roll.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\{1,2,3\}\) represents:
questions.explanation: 1, 2, and 3 are all less than 4.
questions.hint: Compare each outcome in E with the number 4.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret an event from a die roll.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8\}\). The event \(E=\{1,3,5,7\}\) represents:
questions.explanation: 1, 3, 5, and 7 are odd numbers.
questions.hint: Check whether each outcome in E is odd or even.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret an event from a die roll.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8\}\). The event \(E=\{2,4,6,8\}\) represents:
questions.explanation: 2, 4, 6, and 8 are even numbers.
questions.hint: Check whether each outcome in E is odd or even.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an event from an outcome.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{\text{red},\text{blue},\text{green},\text{yellow}\}\). Which of the following is an event?
questions.explanation: An event is a set of outcomes. \(\{\text{red},\text{yellow}\}\) is a set, while red is a single outcome.
questions.hint: An event must be a collection of outcomes.

questions.learningObjective: Check whether a set is a subset of the sample space.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5\}\). The set \(E=\{2,4\}\). Is E an event?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because E is a subset of S.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because E is not a set.

questions.explanation: Any subset of the sample space is an event. E contains only elements of S.
questions.hint: Check whether every element of E belongs to S.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a set is an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5\}\). The set \(E=\{0,2\}\). Is E an event?

options.label: A
options.text: No, because 0 is not in S.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because E has two outcomes.

questions.explanation: An event must be a subset of the sample space. Since 0 is not in S, E is not an event.
questions.hint: Check whether every element of E is in the sample space.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether an event is simple.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{H,T\}\). The event \(E=\{H\}\). Is E a simple event?
questions.explanation: A simple event contains exactly one outcome, and E contains only H.
questions.hint: Count the number of outcomes in E.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a certain event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). This event is:
questions.explanation: E is the entire sample space, so it is certain.
questions.hint: Compare the event with the sample space.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an impossible event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\emptyset\). This event is:
questions.explanation: The empty set has no outcomes, so the event cannot occur.
questions.hint: Think about an event with no elements.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret an event from two coin tosses.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}\). The event \(E=\{HH,TT\}\) represents:
questions.explanation: HH means both heads, and TT means both tails. In both, the tosses match.
questions.hint: Compare the two letters in each outcome of E.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret an event from two coin tosses.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}\). The event \(E=\{HT,TH\}\) represents:
questions.explanation: HT and TH have one head and one tail, so the tosses are different.
questions.hint: Compare the two letters in each outcome of E.

questions.learningObjective: Identify favorable outcomes of an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event is \(E=\{2,3,5\}\). Which outcomes are favorable?
questions.explanation: The favorable outcomes are exactly the elements of E.
questions.hint: List the numbers contained in the event E.

questions.learningObjective: Identify favorable outcomes of an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event is \(E=\{1,4\}\). Which outcomes are favorable?
questions.explanation: The event E contains 1 and 4, so these are the favorable outcomes.
questions.hint: Read the elements directly from E.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether an event is simple.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{\text{red},\text{blue},\text{green}\}\). The event \(E=\{\text{blue}\}\). This event is:
questions.explanation: E contains only one outcome, so it is a simple event.
questions.hint: Count how many outcomes are in E.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether an event is compound.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{\text{red},\text{blue},\text{green}\}\). The event \(E=\{\text{red},\text{blue}\}\). This event is:
questions.explanation: E contains two outcomes, so it is a compound event.
questions.hint: Check whether the event has more than one outcome.

questions.learningObjective: Determine if an outcome is not in an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event is \(E=\{2,4,6\}\). Which outcome is NOT in E?
questions.explanation: 5 is not in E, while 4 is in E.
questions.hint: Find the number that is missing from E.

questions.learningObjective: Determine if an outcome is not in an event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}\). The event is \(E=\{HH,HT\}\). Which outcome is NOT in E?
questions.explanation: TH is not in E, while HH is in E.
questions.hint: Find the outcome that is not listed in E.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a certain event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: E contains every outcome in S, so it is certain.
questions.hint: Compare the event with the entire sample space.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an impossible event.
questions.question: The sample space is \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The event \(E=\emptyset\). Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: The empty set contains no outcomes, so the event cannot occur.
questions.hint: Think about what an event with no elements means.
